emma-support: Pasting a customer report — they hit a tool/function calling failure when proxying to our OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Repro + logs below, customer blocked on a payment flow. Can ENG triage?

emma-support: Customer request (sanitized):
```json
{
  "model": "gpt-4o-mini",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Find product 123"}],
  "tools": [{"name": "Search", "parameters_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"query": {"type": "string"}}}}],
  "function_call": "auto"
}
```

emma-support: Response our API returned to them (snip):
```json
{
  "choices": [{
    "message": {
      "role": "tool",
      "tool_call": {
        "name": "Search",
        "arguments": "{\"query\":\"red widget\"}"
      },
      "content": null
    }
  }]
}
```

emma-support: Our validation throws: `SchemaValidationError: expected object for 'arguments' but got string` — customer says OpenAI returns a stringified arguments field in some SDKs. They also reported mismatch in tool name casing (Search vs search).

raj: Hmm. Two things: enum/case mismatch for tool name and arguments being stringified JSON. Do we currently coerce name -> lowercase before routing? I thought we had a normalizer in oa-compat.

sara-ml: We do a name-alias map (case-insensitive) in the normalizer for the envelope, but that runs after we parse the message->tool_call path assuming `arguments` is an object. If arguments is a string we bail earlier at schema validation.

mike-api: Confirmed from logs — parser tries to jsonschema-validate the tool_call object before running compat normalizers. So stringified args hit the validator and fail.

raj: Possible fixes: 1) run lightweight pre-normalization that JSON-decodes `arguments` if it's a string and looks like JSON; 2) extend validator to accept string and then convert; 3) update docs and SDK warning. Prefer (1) for minimal customer disruption.

sara-ml: Edge cases: if arguments is intentionally a string (some tools expect raw string) then auto-decoding could change semantics. We need to only decode when schema declares `arguments` as object in the tool spec. Also ensure we still enforce max token size after decoding.

mike-api: Implementation plan: add pre-validate shim in oa-compat that: check if message.tool_call.arguments is string AND tool spec says object -> attempt JSON.parse -> if parse fails return compatibility error with helpful message to customer (include example payload). If parse succeeds, set to parsed object and continue. Also add aliasing normalization for `name` (lowercase map) earlier in the path. I can prototype this in the next patch.

emma-support: Customer needs ETA. Can we target a quick patch and hotfix? They are on Dedicated and have an active reserved capacity contract, high priority.

raj: We can do a hotfix branch that only touches the compat shim (no model serving change). Mike, can you sketch a small unit test and a regression case for: (a) stringified args -> parse OK, (b) intentionally string arg -> don't parse if schema expects string, (c) uppercase tool name -> alias map routes to lowercase registered tool.

mike-api: Yup. Tests: add mock tool spec where `arguments` is object; test incoming "arguments":"{\"q\":\"x\"}" -> parsed. Test schema that expects string -> should remain string. I'll open PR after lunch.

sara-ml: Also flagging that evals/regression harness should include a few OpenAI-compatible vendor responses — we've seen multiple variants. I'll add a test vector set.

emma-support: Thanks team. I'll tell customer: patch planned, ETA ~4-8 hours for hotfix + deploy, fallback is a docs snippet showing how to avoid stringifying args. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Deploy task created: oa-compat/pre-parse-arguments-hotfix -> queued for canary.

deploy-bot: Canary scheduled in 30m, notify #eng-oncall if any errors.
